notes.meaning: An earthly high priest is a man chosen from among the people to stand before God on their behalf. His job is to present gifts and sacrifices for sins so people can be restored to God. We can never approach God on our own merit, but only through a priest who represents us.

An earthly priest can treat weak and wandering sinners with gentle patience. He does not act harsh or proud because he struggles with the very same human weaknesses. His own flaws remind him to show mercy to others who lose their way.

Because an earthly priest has sinful flaws, he must bring offerings for his own sins before he can offer gifts for the rest of the people. On the great Day of Atonement, the priest had to confess his own wrongs first. Jesus is far greater because He is completely sinless and needed no sacrifice for Himself.

No person has the right to decide on their own to take up the honor of being high priest. A man had to be called and chosen directly by God, just as Aaron was in the Old Testament. Serving God as a priest is a sacred duty that rests entirely on God's call, not human ambition.

Christ did not push Himself forward or appoint Himself to the role of high priest. Instead, God the Father chose Him and gave Him that glory when He declared Him to be His unique Son. Jesus is fitted for this great work because He shares the very nature of His Father.

God also declared in the Psalms that the Messiah would be a priest forever like Melchizedek. Melchizedek was an ancient king and priest who lived long before Aaron and had no recorded beginning or end to his priesthood. This shows that Jesus serves in an eternal priesthood that never fades away.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics believe Melchizedek's offering of bread and wine foreshadowed Christ instituting the priesthood of the Mass, where Christ's sacrifice is made present under bread and wine.

notes.meaning: While living on earth as a man, Jesus prayed with deep sorrow, loud cries, and tears to the Father who had the power to rescue Him from death. God heard His prayer because Jesus honored the Father with total reverence and trust. Even though He went to the cross, God answered Him by raising Him out of death.

Even though Jesus was God's beloved Son, He learned what obedience feels like through the hard things He suffered. He never sinned or disobeyed, but enduring pain let Him live out obedience in real human experience all the way to the cross. We can trust Him because He knows firsthand how hard it is to obey when life hurts.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that learning through suffering is only God's second-best plan, but commentators reply that Jesus was completely in the Father's perfect will when He suffered.

notes.meaning: By finishing His path of suffering and rising to life, Jesus was fully completed and qualified as our perfect High Priest. He became the eternal source of salvation for everyone who trusts and obeys Him. His work rescues believers forever from sin and judgment.
God officially named Jesus as High Priest in the pattern of Melchizedek. Because Jesus lives forever, His priesthood never changes, and His ability to save us never ends.

The writer has much more to say about Christ and Melchizedek, but it is difficult to explain because the readers have become spiritually lazy. Their hearing has grown dull and slow because they stopped paying careful attention to God's truth. When our hearts grow careless, even wonderful truths become hard to understand.

These believers had been Christians long enough that they should have been ready to teach others by now. Instead, they have fallen behind and need someone to reteach them the very first ABCs of God's word. They have become like little babies who can only drink milk instead of growing people who eat solid food.

Anyone who still lives only on milk is like a little infant who has no teeth for solid food. Such a person is inexperienced in deeper spiritual teachings about God's righteousness. Christians need to grow up in their thinking rather than staying helpless beginners forever.

differ.view: Methodists see milk as basic truths like justification, while the deeper message of righteousness points believers forward to entire sanctification and perfect love.

notes.meaning: Solid food is meant for grown-up believers who are mature in their faith. By constantly putting God's word into practice, they have trained their spiritual senses to tell the difference between good and evil. Regular practice in obeying God helps us spot error and choose what is right.

differ.view: Methodists understand maturity here as reaching a state of Christian perfection where the heart is fully governed by love.
Baptists see this maturity as growth in spiritual knowledge and discernment, holding that no believer attains complete perfection in holiness in this earthly life.
